info.description:
Scientific backend of **MATTER LAB**. It wraps validated scientific libraries (RDKit, and when
installed tblite/xTB and PySCF), runs calculations as asynchronous jobs in worker processes,
keeps reference data with provenance in PostgreSQL, and imports/exports Excel.

Conventions

* Every response is JSON. Errors always have the shape `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}`.
* Coordinates are in angstrom. Energies name their unit in the field name or in a `units` object.
* Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC.
* Results are labelled by how they were obtained (`evidence`) and by the engine and version that
  produced them. Nothing is fabricated: when an engine cannot treat an input the answer is an
  explicit `unsupported` or `failed` state with the reasons.
* An endpoint that needs PostgreSQL answers `503` with code `database_unavailable` while the
  database cannot be reached. An unexpected failure is a `500` with code `internal_error`.
info.title: MATTER LAB science service

post.description:
The ladder is climbed one rung at a time and each rung needs its evidence:
`computationally-plausible` needs an attached calculation that succeeded, converged and was run
on the candidate's structure (and no identical structure in the searched catalogues);
`experimentally-observed` and `independently-validated` need the matching evidence record with
a reference. `structurally-validated` and `no-match-in-searched-catalogs` are set only by the
service. A status can be lowered, but not below what validation and the searches established.
A refused transition answers 409 and says what is missing.

delete.description:
Cancels a queued job immediately. For a running job the worker process is terminated
(SIGTERM, then SIGKILL); the response still shows `running` with `cancel_requested: true` until
the supervisor has confirmed the process is gone, then the status becomes `cancelled`. A job
that is already terminal is returned unchanged. The record itself is kept.
